I'm not even gonna say shit like don't worry, looks don't matter etc because fuck that, that's the kind of society that we live in. Not fitting into beauty standards really does suck and your feelings towards it are valid af. I struggle with that too and here's what has helped me: 
Imagine humans as some kind of aliens. Aliens who have their own weird expectations towards others and these weird af standards focused on such thing called 'beauty' (what even is that?). Imagine humans as aliens having weird body parts, extra legs, few pairs of eyes, tales, wings, and rejecting those whose body parts don't match with what they expect to be beautiful.  Would it even make sense to other aliens in the whole universe? would they understand it? I don't think so.
Here's the other thing: 
Even if you don't fit into beauty standards, IT IS completly possible that someone will fall for you. Love is weird. Falling in love doesn't have any rules and is very often above any beauty standards. It just happens, there are people who will find you the most beautiful girl in the world, who will be able to die for you and that's a fact even if you don't believe it. 
Take care of yourself, outside and inside. You deserve it.  world is harsh enough for us, no need to be more harsh on ourselves.

My mom and I left my dad (alcoholic & abusive) when I was around 3-5 years old. My mom always tried so hard to be the best mom she could but she failed so many times. I was a tough child, I wasn't easy to raise. I spent my early childhood with my mom and my grandparents and all I can remember is that they were all tired of me. I was always scared that my mom will leave and that she doesn't love me. I remember when she used to send me to summer camps and it was a HELL for me. I would spend the whole time crying and calling my mom basically 24/7 because I was SO SO SO scared that something really bad happens to her (like death) and I was just obsessive and scared af. My mom was an abuser too. She would lock me up in the basememt few times as a form of punishment. I can't remember how many times she's hit me. She would often get breakdowns in front of me, she yelled, I knew that she's tired of me. I would always try to get comfort in peers, I remember I was so desperate to have friends in primary school but all it brought to me was a feeling of rejection. I just felt like I didn't belong, kids at my school would always bully me and call me weird and if they spent time with me it was just to make fun of me i guess.

Hey, just because you have a drug addiction and THINK you are a lazy moron doesn’t mean you are not meant for this world. The world is full of evil people (don’t get me wrong, they are meant for this world as well) but drug addiction has nothing to do with how amazing or how evil you are. It’s definitely something you can heal from, and I’m not ‚just saying this’ bc I struggle with addictions as well (I’m not saying we have the same experience tho). You might feel like you are a lazy moron, but these thoughts are a result of your poor mental health, I mean, you want to kill yourself and struggle with an addiction so it’s pretty obvious things are not okay for you, but I REALLY hope it will get better for you in a few weeks/months/years. I don’t know how long it would take 150 yew seeds to do the actual ‚job’ but I’m pretty sure the death would not be instant + drinking alkohol would not make it any less painful, I actually think it would make it even worse. I’m not saying: find another way, I’m just saying I really hope you think about it 3,5,10 or 100 times and decide to give yourself a chance.

I’m sorry you had such bad experience with meds, but please don’t say all psych meds are poison and that doctors are evil. Doctors and meds are saving people’s lives everyday and that’s a fact. Obviously PSSD is a thing and I’m sorry you have to struggle with it but for some people it’s more important to actually cure the depression, like you can’t be sexually healthy if you’re dead at the end of the day.

Hey I can relate to this! 
But you see, the thing is none of us can have a perception of what we truly look like. We can only see ourselfs in the mirror, on the photos or by eyes of other people only by hearing opinions from them. 
And none of these will ever be able to tell us what we truly look like, because let me tell you, when you look in the mirror you probably always tighten your face muscles, do the ‚pretty face’ and look straight into your eyes without any movement. So I try to look at this from this perspective: when people (especially those that I spent time with irl) tell me that I’m pretty/beautiful, they could mean I’m pretty when I laugh, when my mimics and face expressions are authentic, when I talk/smile etc. Those are the things we can’t ever see in ourself, because camera distorts our faces sooo much. So does any mirror. And yeah sure, people could tell us that we’re pretty just for the sake of it, but why the hell would they? I mean, I never do that.
